name: @leewinder/mcp-tcgdex

tools.name: list_card_field_values
tools.description: List the values a card `field` accepts in a language, which search_cards' filters take. `contains` filters them case-insensitively before paging; read further pages while `hasMore` is true. Values come from upstream as they are, so near-identical spellings of one artist can both appear.

language.description: Catalogue language. Names, values and set lists are localised (the Asian catalogues have their own set ids), so look values up in it; prices are the same in every language.

page.description: Zero-indexed page. A page past the end is an empty success with `hasMore` false.

size.description: Results per page; only `hasMore` says whether more exist.

field.description: The card field to list values for. 'type' is a Pokémon card's type (Fire, Water, …); 'energy' is an Energy card's class (Normal or Special); 'category' is the kind of card (Pokemon, Trainer or Energy); 'variant' is a printing the card exists in (normal, holo, reverse, firstEdition).

contains.description: Case-insensitive substring, applied to the whole field before paging, e.g. 'arita' finds 'Mitsuhiro Arita'.

tools.name: list_sets
tools.description: List a language's sets, each with its `id`, `name`, `platform`, `releaseDate`, `serie` and card counts — the values a `set` filter takes. Oldest first unless `sort` or `order` say otherwise: `order` 'desc' lists the newest first. `contains` and `platform` filter the whole catalogue before paging.

language.description: Catalogue language. Names, values and set lists are localised (the Asian catalogues have their own set ids), so look values up in it; prices are the same in every language.

page.description: Zero-indexed page. A page past the end is an empty success with `hasMore` false.

size.description: Results per page; only `hasMore` says whether more exist.

contains.description: Case-insensitive substring of the id or name, applied before paging.

platform.description: 'TCG' for printed sets, 'TCG Pocket' for digital ones; applied before paging. Some catalogues hold only one.

order.description: Whether the order runs ascending or descending — 'desc' on `releaseDate` puts the newest set first.

tools.name: search_cards
tools.description: Search the card catalogue; every filter is optional and they combine with AND. Exact filters (`type`, `energy`, `category`, `trainer`, `stage`, `rarity`, `illustrator`, `variant`, `suffix`, `regulation`) take values from list_card_field_values and match whole, with letter case corrected to the catalogue's — unless two values differ only by case, like suffixes 'EX' and 'ex', which is an error naming both. An unknown value is an error too, so an empty page means real values matched nothing. `name` and `effect` match substrings; `pokemon` finds every card depicting a Pokémon; `attack` and `ability` text is checked over the first 300 matches of the other filters, as `textSearch` reports. Results come in a fixed `sort` order, and `detail` sets how much of each card is returned. Read further pages while `hasMore` is true. Prices come from get_card_pricing, not from cards.

language.description: Catalogue language. Names, values and set lists are localised (the Asian catalogues have their own set ids), so look values up in it; prices are the same in every language.

page.description: Zero-indexed page. A page past the end is an empty success with `hasMore` false.

size.description: Results per page; only `hasMore` says whether more exist.

type.description: Filter by a Pokémon card's type (Fire, Water, …). A dual-type card matches either type.

energy.description: Filter by an Energy card's class (Normal or Special).

category.description: Filter by the kind of card (Pokemon, Trainer or Energy).

trainer.description: Filter by a Trainer card's subtype (Item, Supporter, …).

stage.description: Filter by a Pokémon's evolution stage (Basic, Stage1, …).

rarity.description: Filter by the print rarity ('None' for a card printed without one).

illustrator.description: Filter by the credited artist. Some artists appear under two spellings; list_card_field_values with `contains` shows both.

variant.description: Filter by a printing the card exists in (normal, holo, reverse, firstEdition). True of most cards in several variants at once.

suffix.description: Filter by the name suffix (EX, GX, V, ex, …). Pokémon TCG Pocket's ex cards are recorded as 'EX'.

regulation.description: Filter by the regulation mark letter.

hp.description: Filter by hit points. Both bounds inclusive.

retreat.description: Filter by retreat cost, where 0 is free. Both bounds inclusive.

pokedex.description: Filter by a National Pokédex number. Matches any card depicting it.

pokemon.description: A Pokémon's name in the request language, resolved to its Pokédex number (echoed back) to find every card depicting it.

name.description: Case-insensitive substring of the card name. Names repeat heavily; tell results apart by set and number.

effect.description: Case-insensitive substring of a Trainer or Energy card's effect text.

set.description: Filter to one set by id ('sv04.5') or printed name ('Paldean Fates'), ignoring case; a name several sets share covers them all. list_sets lists both.

platform.description: 'TCG' for printed cards, 'TCG Pocket' for digital ones.

attack.description: Case-insensitive text in an attack's name or effect. Checked over the first 300 matches of the other filters, which it needs at least one of; `textSearch` says whether that covered every match.

ability.description: Case-insensitive text in an ability's name or effect. Checked over the first 300 matches of the other filters, which it needs at least one of; `textSearch` says whether that covered every match.

detail.description: 'summary' (default): identity, set, platform, rarity and images. 'full' adds rules text, legality and every searchable field; it costs about three times the bytes.

sort.description: Order by `id` (default, unique, so pages never overlap) or `name`, alphabetically ignoring case. Cards cannot be ordered by release date.

tools.name: get_set
tools.description: Read one set by id or printed name: its series, release date, platform and card counts, with a page of its cards in printed order as checklist lines of `id`, `localId`, `name` and `rarity`. Call get_card for a card that matters. Legality is per card, from get_card: upstream's set-level flag is wrong for every current set.

language.description: Catalogue language. Names, values and set lists are localised (the Asian catalogues have their own set ids), so look values up in it; prices are the same in every language.

page.description: Zero-indexed page. A page past the end is an empty success with `hasMore` false.

size.description: Results per page; only `hasMore` says whether more exist.

set.description: The set to read, as id ('sv04.5') or printed name ('Paldean Fates'), ignoring case; a name several sets share covers them all. list_sets lists both.

tools.name: get_card
tools.description: Read one whole card by its `id`, or by its `set` and the number printed on it, `localId` — not both. The set may be an id or a printed name, ignoring case, and leading zeros in the number are optional. Returns the shape search_cards gives at `detail` 'full'. A card that does not exist is an error saying whether the set or the number was wrong.

language.description: Catalogue language. Names, values and set lists are localised (the Asian catalogues have their own set ids), so look values up in it; prices are the same in every language.

id.description: Global card id, e.g. 'swsh3-136'. Give it alone; take it from a search_cards or get_set result rather than composing one.

set.description: The card's set, given with `localId`: id ('sv04.5') or printed name ('Paldean Fates'), ignoring case; a name several sets share covers them all. list_sets lists both.

localId.description: The number printed on the card, e.g. '105'; leading zeros are optional. Give it with `set`, not with `id`.

tools.name: get_card_pricing
tools.description: Price up to 50 cards in EUR, USD or GBP, from Cardmarket (EUR) and TCGplayer (USD) side by side, with one total per market — never blended, since one is a trend and the other a market price. Name each card by `id`, or by `set` and `localId`, with an optional `variant` and `quantity`. Each line's `status` is `priced`; `unpriced`; `ambiguous`, when no `variant` was named and the copy held is unclear — name one of its `variants`; or `unavailable`, when the card could not be read or the line is malformed, which never fails the call. A missing price gives a `reason`: `no_listing`, `variant_unpriced`, `variant_not_printed`, `separate_product` (sold as a product of its own and unpriced here, like Base Set's 1st Edition or a Poké Ball reverse), `window_unavailable`, `platform_unpriced`, `unavailable` or `unrecognised_shape`. `approximateVariant` marks a price that may cover more than the printing named, and `separatelyListedPrintings` counts printings sold separately. Each price has its native `amount` and a `convertedAmount` at the ECB rate in `exchangeRates.rates`. A total is `complete` only when every line is priced. `warnings` flag markets more than 10× apart for a printing, and stale rates. Prices are for one copy in unspecified condition, before fees, and the same in every language.

language.description: Catalogue language. Names, values and set lists are localised (the Asian catalogues have their own set ids), so look values up in it; prices are the same in every language.

id.description: Global card id, e.g. 'swsh3-136'. Give it alone; take it from a search_cards or get_set result rather than composing one.

set.description: The card's set, given with `localId`: id ('sv04.5') or printed name ('Paldean Fates'), ignoring case; a name several sets share covers them all. list_sets lists both.

localId.description: The number printed on the card, e.g. '105'; leading zeros are optional. Give it with `set`, not with `id`.

variant.description: The printing, matched ignoring case: one of the examples, where 'firstEdition' means the card's 1st Edition. Name the edition of a vintage card. Omit it to list every printing, which is ambiguous unless there is only one.

quantity.description: Copies held; multiplies the totals, never the prices shown.

cards.description: One line per card, named the way get_card names one. A bad line is reported as unavailable; it never fails the call.

currency.description: The currency to convert to. Each price is also given in its market's own currency.

basis.description: Which figure to read. 'market' is TCGplayer's market price and Cardmarket's trend; 'low' the lowest listing; the day averages are Cardmarket's alone. TCGplayer gives `window_unavailable` for an average.

tools.name: rank_card_prices
tools.description: Rank the cards matching `name`, `pokemon`, `pokedex`, `set` or `rarity` — at least one, matched as in search_cards — by one market's price, most valuable first unless `order` is 'asc'. Each card is ranked once, by its highest-priced printing in `rankMarket`: a row in `cards` gives that `variant`, its `price`, and the other market's price as `otherMarket`. Upstream cannot sort by price, so the first 300 matches are read; `truncated` says more matched, and `coverage` accounts for every card read, counting unpriced ones by the same `reason` codes get_card_pricing uses. `separatelyListedPrintings` counts printings sold separately and not ranked. A row's `warnings` flag markets more than 10× apart; the order still follows `rankMarket`. Prices show the native `amount` and a `convertedAmount` at the rate in `exchangeRates.rates`, for one copy in unspecified condition, before fees.

language.description: Catalogue language. Names, values and set lists are localised (the Asian catalogues have their own set ids), so look values up in it; prices are the same in every language.

name.description: Case-insensitive substring of the card name. Names repeat heavily; tell results apart by set and number.

pokemon.description: A Pokémon's name in the request language, resolved to its Pokédex number (echoed back) to find every card depicting it.

pokedex.description: Filter by a National Pokédex number. Matches any card depicting it.

set.description: Filter to one set by id ('sv04.5') or printed name ('Paldean Fates'), ignoring case; a name several sets share covers them all. list_sets lists both.

rarity.description: Filter by the print rarity ('None' for a card printed without one).

currency.description: The currency to show prices in; it never changes the order. Each price is also given in its market's own currency.

basis.description: Which figure to rank by. 'market' is TCGplayer's market price and Cardmarket's trend; 'low' the lowest listing; the day averages are Cardmarket's alone. So an average needs `rankMarket` 'cardmarket'.

rankMarket.description: The one market whose price orders the ranking; each row shows the other's too.

limit.description: How many rows to return; fewer when fewer cards have a price.

instructions: This server reads the TCGdex Pokémon Trading Card Game catalogue. Filter values are localised and drawn from fixed lists: look them up with list_card_field_values, and sets with list_sets, in the language you search in. Use search_cards to find cards, get_set to walk a set, and get_card to read one card by `id`, or by `set` and `localId`. Lists are paged: request further pages while `hasMore` is true. In a card, a `rarity` of null means it was printed without one, while no `rarity` means the catalogue records none; `damage` is printed text; and a missing `cost` may be a gap in the data rather than a free attack. No card carries prices: get_card_pricing prices cards you can name and rank_card_prices ranks a search, both showing Cardmarket (EUR) and TCGplayer (USD) side by side and converting at the latest ECB rate.
